Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
Absolutely! Here's a simple breakdown of the main spirit categories we offer:
Whiskey — The umbrella term for spirits made from grains and aged in barrels. We carry over 20,000 spirits from around the world.
Main types:
Bourbon — American whiskey made with at least 51% corn, giving it a sweet, smooth flavor with notes of vanilla and caramel. It's aged in new charred oak barrels, which gives it that warm, amber color.
Scotch — Whiskey made in Scotland. The ones I showed you earlier (Johnnie Walker) are blended Scotch — smooth and balanced, great for beginners.
Rye — Spicier, bolder whiskey made primarily from rye grain.
Other spirits we carry:
Tequila — Made from agave in Mexico, ranges from smooth to complex
Rum — Made from sugarcane, often sweet and tropical
Gin — Botanical spirit with juniper flavor
Vodka — Neutral, clean spirit

Great question! Here's what you actually need to get started as a beginner:
The essentials:
1. Proper glassware — You'll want at least one tasting glass. A Glencairn glass or small sherry glass is ideal for any spirit, as it allows you to properly savor and smell the whiskey's aroma (a regular tumbler doesn't work as well for this).
2. Water — Have plenty of water on hand to alternate sips and clear your palate. Adding a bit of water to your whiskey can also open up the spirit and take the edge off the alcohol, helping you detect finer notes. Use spring water or soft tap water that won't add its own flavor. Skip the ice if you're really tasting the whiskey.
3. Snacks (optional) — Unflavored, unsalted crackers or small slices of bread help cleanse your palate between sips.
The good news: You probably already have water and crackers at home! The only thing you might want to add is proper glassware:

How do I use it properly the very first time?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Perfect question! Here's exactly how to taste whiskey properly for the first time:
Step 1: The Aroma (Nose)
Gently bring the glass up to your nose — don't rush this! You don't want to overwhelm your nose. Some people even nose spirits with one nostril first, then both. Take your nose away from the glass after each sniff, trust the first thing you smell, then repeat and other layers will slowly reveal themselves. Try to name the familiar smells — this takes practice. After a while, give your nose a break with some fresh air and water.
Step 2: The Taste (Palate)
Take a small sip and roll the spirit over your tongue and around its sides, then throughout your mouth. Savor the flavors and start identifying them — are they weak or strong? Herbal? Woody? Fruity? Spicy? Take note of the mouth-feel, which refers to both the texture and intensity of the spirit.
Step 3: Add Water (Optional)
After your first taste, try adding just a tiny bit of water. This can open up the spirit and help you detect finer notes.
For Maker's Mark specifically, expect:
Sweet vanilla and caramel notes
Smooth, velvety texture
Gentle warmth (not harsh)
Pro tip: Don't feel pressure to identify every flavor on your first try. Just notice what you like and don't like. Your palate will develop over time!
